newsitem.title: SOMALIA: 100 militiamen defect in Mogadishu, witnesses say.
newsitem.headline: 100 militiamen defect in Mogadishu, witnesses say.

text.p: Some 100 militiamen crossed the "Green Line" battle zone dividing Mogadishu and defected to Somali faction leader Hussein Aideed in the south, witnesses said on Wednesday.
The mass defection from north Mogadishu faction leader Ali Mahdi Mohamed was believed to be the largest ever in the city.
Witnesses said the militiamen, armed with assault rifles, strolled across the Green Line on Tuesday in broad daylight and were welcomed by Aideed's commanders at his headquarters.
Political sources said the defection was arranged by a former Ali Mahdi official who defected to Aideed last year.
Ali Mahdi left Ethiopia for Mogadishu on Wednesday in a bid to persuade Aideed and Mohamed Ibrahim Egal, the president of the self-declared republic of Somaliland, to attend talks in November.

A spokesman in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa for an alliance of 26 factions led by Ali Mahdi said he would meet Aideed on Friday to try to persuade him to attend the reconciliation talks in Bosasso town in northeast Somalia.
He said Ali Mahdi would then travel to northwestern Somalia in an attempt to persuade Egal to go to the talks.
Egal and Aideed boycotted talks in Ethiopia which led to the 26 factions forming a National Salvation Council before the Bosasso meeting to set up a provisional government for the country.
Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow of its late dictator and president Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991.
